subject: Private deployments: audit logging parity plan (schema v1 + sensitive actions coverage)
body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Private deployments: audit logging parity plan (schema v1 + sensitive actions coverage)

Team — following up on the Private-side parity expectation for audit logging.

We need a single, unambiguous definition we can use for:
1) engineering acceptance (what’s “done” for Private), and
2) customer-facing language (what we can safely commit to in security reviews).

Proposed parity definition (Private vs Hosted/Dedicated):
- For any action in the “sensitive actions” taxonomy, Private emits an audit event with the same event_type, same required fields, and schema_version tagging.
- Equivalent actions should have equivalent semantics (actor/target/resource), even if the underlying mechanics differ (installer vs control plane API).
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once is acceptable, but we must provide de-dupe guidance via event_id.

Attached is a first pass checklist I pulled together from the installer flows + the recurring customer complaints (SUP-18421) and what Security/GRC have been asking for.

Asks:
- Marcus/Naomi: can you confirm (or adjust) what we’re willing to state externally about delivery guarantees and “100% coverage” for Private?
- Priya: can we confirm a realistic rollout schedule so we’re not over-rotating in customer conversations?
- Olga: please sanity-check any wording that impacts SOC2 evidence language.

Attachments:
- private-audit-logging-parity-checklist-v0.3.pdf (draft)
- private-audit-logging-rollout-milestones-v1.txt (draft)

Thanks,
Vivek

—
Vivek Kulkarni
PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 10:04 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private deployments: audit logging parity plan (schema v1 + sensitive actions coverage)

+1 to locking this down.

On external language: I want us to be very crisp that “coverage” means: for each sensitive action, we emit an event with stable semantics + the v1 schema (and that we’re actively instrumenting remaining gaps). We should avoid phrasing that implies:
- synchronous writes (i.e., “logged before action completes”), or
- exactly-once delivery.

I’d suggest customer-safe phrasing along the lines of:
- “Audit events are delivered with at-least-once semantics; consumers should de-duplicate using event_id.”
- “In the event of downstream delivery delays, events may arrive late; Redwood monitors delivery latency and drop rate.”

Also: the checklist should explicitly call out a couple of “gotchas” that customers ask about:
- operator identity for installer actions (when it’s available vs not),
- source IP / origin context for Private actions (what we can capture reliably in air-gapped),
- and redaction rules (no secrets, no raw API keys).

I’ll let Marcus weigh in on the delivery guarantee sentence.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
PM, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private deployments: audit logging parity plan (schema v1 + sensitive actions coverage)

Agree with Naomi.

Two points to tighten:

1) Delivery semantics
We should standardize the statement to:
- “At-least-once delivery” (duplicates possible)
- “Best effort not acceptable for sensitive actions” (i.e., producers should buffer/retry locally where feasible)
- “If the audit sink is unavailable, the action may still proceed, but the event must be queued and delivered when connectivity returns” (where supported)

We can’t promise global durability in all Private footprints (e.g., fully air-gapped, storage constraints), so the external statement needs a qualifier. Internally we can enforce stronger requirements in our supported reference architecture.

2) Parity definition
I’d add one more bullet: “Parity includes correlation fields (request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id) wherever the action originates from a Redwood control plane/API request.”

For installer-driven flows:
- If there is no request context, we should still emit a stable operator identity field when the operator is authenticated (or set actor_type=system with actor_id=unknown and a clear reason string).

Net: I’m aligned to treat this as a release gate for Private once we declare the sensitive actions list final.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering (Exec Owner)
Redwood Inference

On schedule / milestones (assuming no surprises in validation across Hosted + Private):

- Week of Feb 10–14:
  - finalize schema v1 + taxonomy docs for service owners
  - Private checklist locked (Vivek owner)

- Week of Feb 17–21:
  - private-installer emits v1 events for install/upgrade/rollback/config apply (ENG-4826)
  - schema_version tagging + normalization in exporter (ENG-4827) starts rollout in Private reference configs

- Week of Feb 24–28:
  - fill remaining gaps for Private-specific sensitive actions (credential rotation, export config changes, data retention/residency settings)
  - first pass E2E validation in Private fixture environment (smoke, then targeted)

- Week of Mar 2–6:
  - enable coverage dashboard sampling for Private tenants (internal-only first)
  - readiness review: known exclusions require explicit waiver + expiry

Customer comms:
- I’d prefer we tell customers “rolling out in February/March” rather than commit to an exact date until the exporter normalization is proven in a couple real deployments.

Resourcing is good on Platform/SecEng for the above, but we need Private team availability for testing on real upgrade paths.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Platform Org Sponsor

Subject: Re: Private deployments: audit logging parity plan (schema v1 + sensitive actions coverage)

GRC perspective:

- I’m supportive of the “at-least-once + de-dupe via event_id” language. That’s consistent with what auditors accept as long as we:
  (a) document it, and
  (b) show monitoring/alerting for delivery failures.

- Please do NOT say “100% coverage” externally until we can produce:
  - the taxonomy list (final),
  - evidence that the main sensitive workflows emit events (sample queries/screenshots), and
  - the exception/waiver process for anything not yet covered.

Suggested customer-safe wording:
- “Redwood provides audit logging for sensitive administrative actions with a versioned schema. Coverage is continuously expanding; Redwood can share the current event taxonomy and guidance for export and de-duplication.”

Also: the checklist attachment is helpful; can we add a simple “evidence mapping” column (which control family / what evidence artifact) so we can reuse it for SOC2/ISO packets?

Olga

—
Olga Petrov
GRC Lead

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Private deployments: audit logging parity plan (schema v1 + sensitive actions coverage)

Thanks all — synthesizing into a plan we can socialize with the Private eng leads and keep consistent in customer threads.

Decisions / alignment:
- Parity definition (Private):
  - same event_type + required fields + schema_version as Hosted/Dedicated for equivalent sensitive actions
  - include correlation IDs where there is request context (request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id)
  - for installer-only actions, emit actor context when available; otherwise explicit actor_type=system + actor_id=unknown with a reason note

- Delivery semantics (customer-safe):
  - at-least-once delivery; duplicates possible; recommend de-dupe by event_id
  - avoid “exactly-once” / “synchronous write” language
  - include qualifier that durability depends on the supported reference architecture in Private (esp. air-gapped)

- External positioning:
  - do not claim “100% coverage” until we can show taxonomy + evidence + exception process
  - we can say “versioned schema” + “sensitive admin actions” + “SIEM export guidance” now

Next steps:
1) I’ll update the checklist (add evidence mapping column per Olga + callouts re operator identity/source IP constraints) and resend as v0.4.
2) Priya’s milestones look right — I’ll translate into the Private release notes language (rolling Feb/Mar; no hard dates).
3) Marcus/Naomi: once the updated checklist is out, can you both sign off on a 4–5 sentence customer-facing paragraph we can reuse in security reviews?

Vivek
